notes.decision: Translated 'the manner also: only-begottens' — ⲧⲥⲉ functions as the discourse-typological marker 'the manner/the way' (cf. ⲧⲛⲟ/ⲡⲛⲟ in glossary) introducing parallel applications. The disciples are addressed as μονογενεῖς in multiple registers — by kind, by flesh, by gold/fire/wealth.

Left as lacuna with visible ⲉⲙⲗⲁ. The form is unidentified; could be a corrupted Greek loanword (perhaps κειμήλια 'treasures' or χρῆμα 'wealth') given the gold/fire context, but no secure reading. The phrase ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ ⲙⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'all of the cosmos' modifies it.

Translated 'molder of men' as agent-noun on the same root as ⲡⲱⲁⲡⲧ 'the molding/fashioning' (in glossary). The cosmological context — standing alone in the midst of all worlds of darkness, not loving the worlds of darkness — corresponds precisely to the descent of First Man (ⲡⲱⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ). The figure may be a typological compression: First Man as cosmic prototype-molder of humanity. Alternative: 'molded one of men.' Confidence moderate.

Translated 'the giving toward his men' — ⲙ-ⲧⲏⲓ̈ as verbal noun of ϯ 'give' (ⲡⲧⲏⲓ̈ 'the giving') paired with ⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ 'love.' The Father's love is constituted by his giving toward humanity — the soteriological economy of light-redemption.

Translated 'teachings of force ... he is bitter and harsh.' ⲭⲛⲁⲥ = ϫⲛⲁⲥ 'force/violence' (cf. ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲝⲓⲛⲟⲁⲛⲥ̄ in glossary). ϥ̄ⲥⲁⲥⲉ = qualitative 'is bitter' (cf. ⲥⲓϣⲉ). ϩⲥⲱⲭⲉ tentatively rendered 'harsh' — possibly Lyc. for ⲍⲥⲱⲭⲉ from ⲥⲱϣ 'scorn' or ϩⲱϫ 'oppress.'
Translated 'shall cast them forth' — Lyc. ⲛⲟⲩⲭ (= ⲛⲟⲩϫⲉ 'cast') with future ⲛⲁ- and 3pl object suffix.

Translated 'they shall restore them' — ⲣ̄-ⲧⲥⲉ tentatively analyzed as a Lyc. compound on ⲧⲥⲟ 'establish, set' or ⲧⲥⲁⲃⲟ 'instruct.' The cosmological-soteriological context (returning to original place 'from the beginning') supports a restoration/return verb. Could alternatively be 'they shall instruct them.'

Translated 'let them celebrate the remembrance of giving' — jussive ⲙⲁⲣⲟⲩ- + ⲟⲩⲟⲛ (likely 'open up, perform' here in cultic-mnemonic register), with the substantivized ⲣ̄ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'commemoration' (in glossary). The exhortation calls the disciples to commemorative acts of giving.

Translated 'Concerning the Two Substances.' ⲧⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ takes the feminine article on the Greek loanword ⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ; ⲥⲛⲧⲉ = 'two' (fem.). The chapter title is flanked by the chapter number ⲣⲕ̄ (120) on both sides, a standard Kephalaia heading-bracket convention.

Translated 'our Father examined.' ⲙⲟⲩⲥ = Lyc. variant of ⲙⲟⲩⲍ/ⲙⲟⲩϣⲧ̄ 'examine, scrutinize' (cf. ⲙⲟⲩⲍ in accumulated vocabulary), here with ⲥ for ⲍ. The dialogue-frame opens with the Apostle's examination of his disciples or audience.

Translated 'Two substances are those existing from the beginning' — the foundational Manichaean dualist proposition opening this kephalaion. ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲣⲭⲏ = 'from the beginning' (Greek ἀρχή with directional ⲛ̄-).
Translated 'every thing.' ⲥⲱⲃ = Lyc. ϩⲱⲃ 'thing, work' (with ⲥ for ϩ — unusual but consistent with this manuscript's occasional ⲥ/ⲍ alternation for standard Coptic ϩ).
